title: Run loop and the main thread
summary: The main thread runs a loop: wait for events (touches, timers), handle them, then draw the UI changes, then sleep. If your code on main is slow, the next frame is late and the app stutters.
body: **In simple words:** The main run loop is an endless loop: "Is there a touch? A timer? A block on the main queue? Handle it. Now update the screen. Nothing to do? Sleep until something happens."
**Real-life analogy:** A receptionist with one desk. They take calls, visitors and letters one at a time. If one visitor takes 5 minutes, everyone else waits - that is a frozen UI.
**Frame budget:** at 60 Hz the screen refreshes every 16.7 ms; at 120 Hz (ProMotion) every ~8 ms. Your main-thread work per frame must fit in that, or the frame is dropped (a hitch).
**Modes:** while you scroll, the run loop switches to `.tracking` mode. A `Timer` added in `.default` mode pauses while scrolling. Add it to `.common` modes to keep it firing.

**Where your code runs:** `@MainActor` code, `DispatchQueue.main.async` blocks and UIKit callbacks all run on this loop. UI changes are collected and committed to the render server at the end of the loop iteration (Core Animation transaction).
keyPoints: Main run loop = event loop: input sources, timers, main-queue work, then UI commit.
Frame budget ~16 ms (60 Hz) or ~8 ms (120 Hz); slow main work = hitches.
Timer in `.common` mode keeps firing during scroll.
A hang = main thread blocked ≥ 250 ms; watchdog kills apps blocked too long at launch.

code.caption: Timer that keeps firing during scroll
code.text:
let timer = Timer(timeInterval: 1, repeats: true) { _ in updateCountdown() }
RunLoop.main.add(timer, forMode: .common)

mistakes: Doing JSON parsing, image decoding or disk I/O on main.
followups: **Do background threads have run loops?** Each thread has one, but it only runs if you start it; GCD threads normally do not need it.
**Why does my timer stop during scrolling?** It is scheduled in `.default` mode.
